devs.title: Mainspring in Nivaflex 45/5
devs.period: Straumann's Nivaflex: patented 1948, the name registered 1957
devs.vmat: Nivaflex 45/5 (Co 45, Ni 21, Cr 18, Fe 5, W 4, Mo 4, Ti 1, Be 0.2 %)
devs.vtreat: cold-drawn strip 0.386 mm thick (0.379-0.400 keeps the manual's swing) × 13.55 mm × 1064 mm, aged 2 h at 500 °C to over 3000 N/mm²; coiled; greased
devs.why: The same torque from a strip 0.386 mm thick (E 220 GPa against carbon steel's 207), so the fusee, the swing and the rate are unchanged. Fully wound it is stressed 2309 MPa, a margin of 1.30 on Nivaflex's 3000 N/mm² against carbon steel's 1.13-1.17; it doesn't take a set, rust in salt air or magnetize, so its pull, and with it the rate, holds steady over the months a navigator carries it.
sources: Jacques Allemann, Nivaflex 45/5 data sheet JAS-014 (2021): composition, E 220 GPa, density 8.50, expansion 11.2 × 10⁻⁶/K, strength over 3000 N/mm², non-magnetic, corrosion
Vacuumschmelze, Nivaflex 45/18 brochure: tensile strength up to 2900 MPa, hardness up to 800 HV, mainsprings among its uses
Nivaflex, Wikipedia; R. Straumann, Grail-Watch wiki: patented 1948, Nivaflex SA, the name registered 1957

devs.title: Balance in Glucydur, hairspring in Nivarox
devs.period: Glucydur (beryllium bronze, 1930s) and Nivarox (Straumann, perfected 1933, patented 1935), offered together by 1940

vmat.42188: Nivarox (Fe-Ni-Cr-Be, self-compensating), graded to the balance

vtreat.42178: turned and hardened (about 400 HB); the rim uncut; poised, the screws as drawn
vtreat.42188: the same helix and terminal curves (hairspring.js), the strip 0.215-0.228 mm × 0.23 mm; its thermoelastic coefficient graded to 4 to 14 × 10⁻⁶ a °C for the made balance (within ±1.4); vibrated to the balance, its length taken at the stud

devs.why: A monometallic bronze balance with a self-compensating spring replaces a balance of two metals and an Elinvar spring whose heat treatment must be matched to it: the spring is bought graded to the balance, the temperature error trimmed on the bench, and the balance is turned in one piece on the CNC. The balance comes out 2-6 % heavier for its shape, which the spring's length takes up; the spring must cancel the bronze's expansion, 4 to 14 × 10⁻⁶ a °C, within ±1.4 to meet the Navy's temperature figure. The density and expansion are beryllium bronze's (CuBe2), Nivarox's expansion and modulus estimated: the temperature test (the bench's last) settles it.
sources: Glucydur, Wikipedia; Horopedia: beryllium bronze with iron, about 400 HB, non-magnetic, for balances
Xometry, beryllium bronze C17200 data sheet: density 8.25 g/cm³, expansion 17 × 10⁻⁶/°C

Nivarox, Wikipedia; WatchesbySJX, "Hairspring Materials and Evolution Part II" (2025); VintageWatchstraps, "Nivarox balance springs": Fe-Ni-Cr-Be, its thermoelastic coefficient set by alloy and heat treatment, positive for monometallic balances; perfected 1933, patented 1935
The manual (Sec. II): the Model 21's stainless rim, Invar arm and Elinvar spring
